note: EVERY top-level route under frontend/app is classified here, once. Operator 2026-10-14 (DD-55): 'each innovation project gets its own rcore panel (drone, security, light codex, Vision-2525, etc)', and asked what counts: 'all projects that are off main. /project-2525'. A pure route-shape rule cannot be the test on its own — 26 top-level routes carry a page and sixteen of them are utilities — so the rule survives in a stronger form: every route is CLASSIFIED here, and a row classified 'project' must have a ledger, a panel and (when the code record lands) a code record. The gate then never guesses; the row is the decision, and a 'utility' row must say why in one line, so an exclusion is on the record rather than in someone's head. Append-only in spirit: change a row rather than dropping it, and say why in its own note.

kinds.project: An innovation project off main. MUST have: its own append-only ledger under docs/traceability, a mounted R-CORE badge + panel over that ledger, and (DD-53) a code record per revision.
kinds.alias: A second address for a project that is already classified. Renders the SAME component, so it inherits that project's panel and must NOT have a ledger of its own — one record per project, never two.
kinds.surface: Part of a project rather than a project: a reader, a viewer or a sub-page reached from one. It inherits its project's record.
kinds.utility: Not a project: a function of the app (auth, joining, a session, a redirect). No ledger, no panel. Every utility row carries a one-line why.

routes.excludeWhy: The carried drone-2525_r.NNN.html files are byte-identical COPIES of frontend/public/drone-2525/play.html (tests/drone-playable.test.mjs asserts it), so counting them measures the same change twice at 1.1 MB a go; docs/drone-2525/exports/ is generated by scripts/drone-render.mjs from the domain JSON. Both are excluded from the code record so an area's diff is the change, not its duplicates.
routes.areasWhy: Operator 2026-10-15: "make sure drone pieces allow for future modularization, 1v1, 3v3" and "different maps like capital lawn, City of Austin, State of Texas". The map ladder, each map rung and the match/team layer each hold their OWN piece from the start - austin and texas light nothing yet, and that is the point: the cube shows the project's whole anatomy, dim where a piece is declared but not built, so building it lights an existing piece instead of re-cutting the cube.
